en: Taal Volcano features Vulcan Point, a small island located inside a lake that sits within the crater of a larger volcano.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River is a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea, experiencing tidal influences.
Bohol's Chocolate Hills consist of exactly 1,268 symmetrical, cone-shaped limestone mounds that turn chocolate brown during the dry season.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines and the third largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia.
Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for having the most perfectly symmetrical volcanic cone in the entire world.
The Verde Island Passage, located between Batangas and Mindoro, contains the highest concentration of marine shorefish biodiversity globally.
Although the Philippines is an archipelago of 7,641 islands, only about 2,000 of these islands are permanently inhabited.
The Galathea Depth in the Philippine Trench is the third deepest oceanic trench point in the entire world.
Mount Hamiguitan in Davao Oriental features a unique, century-old pygmy forest where trees grow only a few meters tall.
The northernmost province of Batanes is geographically closer to Taiwan than it is to the Philippine capital of Manila.
If the ancient Banaue Rice Terraces in the Cordilleras were laid end to end, they would encircle half the globe.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo was the second largest volcanic eruption on Earth during the entire twentieth century.
